background_details.current_setup: Wyze Cam Outdoor v2 on rental unit porches, Eufy Video Doorbell (battery) on home front door, Schlage Encode Plus on home and two rental units, Ring Alarm 8-piece kit at one rental
background_details.relevant_history: Has installed and managed security gear across 4 properties over 7+ years — own home plus 3 rental units. Has replaced equipment after tenant damage, compatibility issues, and subscription fatigue. Learned no-drill and renter-friendly constraints from necessity.

product_experiences.notes: Reliable, affordable, local storage via microSD, no mandatory subscription — fits the rental use case well. Battery life shorter than advertised in cold weather.
Hardware is solid; professional monitoring subscription adds up across multiple properties. Self-monitored mode works fine for most use cases.
Retrofit fits most deadbolts without drilling new holes. Guest code management is genuinely practical for rental turnover.
Very long battery life, but local storage requires the Blink Sync Module 2 — often missed in initial purchase. Cloud storage has a mandatory subscription for multi-camera setups.

failures.reason: Subscription-dependent for key features (activity zones, e2e encryption) — cost across multiple units becomes significant. Replaced with lower-subscription-burden alternatives.
Required proprietary hub that was discontinued. Lost remote access capability. Lesson: check manufacturer track record before committing across multiple properties.

strong_opinions: Subscription cost compounds across multiple properties — what seems negligible for one unit is a real line item across four.
Local storage (microSD or NVR) is almost always worth the slightly higher upfront cost vs. cloud-only cameras for landlords.
Renter usability matters more than features — if a tenant can't figure out how to share access, the smart lock becomes a support call.
Professional monitoring is rarely necessary for rental units where you're checking footage after the fact, not responding in real time.
No-drill installation is a hard requirement for rentals in many markets — lease terms or local ordinances prohibit permanent mounting.
voice_samples: The subscription math changes completely when you're running it across four properties.
I've replaced gear that worked fine technically but that tenants couldn't figure out — usability is part of reliability.
The spec says six-month battery life. Owners in colder climates report two to three months. That's the gap I weight.
If you need a professional installer for initial setup, it's already a problem for my use case.
Ring's professional monitoring is legitimately useful for some homeowners. For most of my rental units, the self-monitored option covers everything that actually matters.
